title: The bridged cross-polytope framework: unit-spring elastic constants in every dimension and an exact motion from the CaB6 boron net to face-centred cubic packing
description: Version 2, superseding v1 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23322080), whose novelty claims for the rigidity counts are corrected. For the periodic framework of regular cross-polytopes joined by bars (the same periodic graph as Borcea and Streinu 2021, Section 7), we prove that with unit springs every shear modulus vanishes, C11/C12 = (n-1)^2 and the Poisson ratio is 1/(n^2-n-1), for every dimension n >= 3; the zero-mode and self-stress counts are lemmas following from existing periodic-rigidity machinery. In three dimensions we give an exact continuous motion, rational in one parameter over Q(sqrt2), that keeps every bar length, holds the octahedra in fixed orientation while the lattice deforms, raises the packing density strictly from 0.2233 to pi/sqrt18 and ends at face-centred cubic packing, with non-overlap proven. Secondary results: a radius-ratio identity and the exact CaB6-type packing maximum. The archive contains the preprint, the interactive site, replayable verifiers and certificates. Not peer reviewed.
notes: Computation, proofs, checking and writing were carried out with AI assistance under the author's direction: Claude Opus 5.5 and other Claude models (Anthropic); GPT-6 (Codex), GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna (OpenAI) for the continuous fcc motion, the CaB6 attainment proof, the certificate registry, the literature audit, the research assessment and the October 2026 site update. See CONTRIBUTORS.md for which model did what.
